I farm in Quzhou County, so I will follow the pattern that fits my land, my age, and what I know how to manage steadily. I will keep my main land in the winter wheat and summer maize rotation, because that is the most reliable way for me to use the full year, spread risk, and make use of the irrigation and field habits I already have. I am 64, so I will not choose crops that need too much hand labor or complicated market timing. I want crops I can manage with familiar operations, stable inputs, and predictable buyers.

For the winter side, I will keep wheat on the better land because it handles our local system well and gives me a solid first harvest. I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed, because I want more even emergence and better yield without making management too complicated. I will fertilize enough to support yield but not push too hard, because too much nitrogen raises lodging and disease risk. I will irrigate a few key times instead of too often, focusing on the stages that matter most. I will use rotary tillage after the summer crop to prepare a workable seedbed without making the work too heavy.

After wheat, I will plant summer maize. That is the crop I trust most after wheat in this area. I will use hybrid seed because maize responds well to it and gives me stronger yield. I will apply more nitrogen to maize than wheat, because maize needs it more strongly in our double-cropping system. I will keep phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels and manage weeds and insects with a limited number of sprays instead of many passes. I will keep irrigation to the main critical periods and not overdo it. This way I keep the system practical, productive, and within the level of work I am willing to carry through the whole year.
